errors.english: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder] and the nirvana without remainder
errors.why: The two final fruits are the nirvana with remainder and the nirvana without remainder; the English calls the first 'remainderless' while its own note says 'with remainder', so the pair is confused.

note: Faithful rendering of the commentary's preamble on purpose and connection; only the naming of the two nirvanas is muddled.

errors.english: Om, I am the nature of all the Tathagatas
errors.why: svabhāva tvaṃ is 'you are the nature of all Tathāgatas', addressed to the disciple like the following clauses.

fix.find: Om, I am the nature of all the Tathagatas
fix.replace: Om, you are the nature of all the Tathagatas

errors.why: The four assistants and four samaya consorts also take up the vases of Vairocana and the others (continued on the next side); 'represent' is supplied and misconstrues the sentence.

note: A clear account of the sequence of consecrations; the mantra addressed to the disciple is turned into a first-person statement.

errors.english: one satisfies the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening in each and every moment
errors.why: lhan cig: the enjoyment body is itself satisfied together with the bodhisattvas at every moment; the bodhisattvas are not the object being satisfied.

fix.find: one satisfies the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening in each and every moment
fix.replace: one is satisfied, together with the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening, in each and every moment

errors.english: just as mentioning "Vajrabhairava" allows one to know the entire class of Bhairava deities
errors.why: This is the grammarians' stock example of a shortened name: saying 'Bhīma' one understands 'Bhīmasena'; it has nothing to do with Vajrabhairava or a class of deities.

fix.find: just as mentioning "Vajrabhairava" allows one to know the entire class of Bhairava deities
fix.replace: just as by saying "Bhīma" one understands "Bhīmasena"

errors.english: through the application of inspired energy
errors.why: spro ba here is emanation: samaya 'goes everywhere' through the practice of emanating (forms), not through 'inspired energy'.

note: The etymologies of mahāsattva and samayasattva are handled well, but the grammatical example and who is satisfied are wrong.

errors.english: The measure of merit is such that it excludes everyone except a Bodhisattva who is close to enlightenment.
errors.why: The measure of one merit is as much as all the enjoyment-yielding merit of beings, EXCLUDING bodhisattvas near awakening; the English inverts the exclusion.

fix.find: The measure of merit is such that it excludes everyone except a Bodhisattva who is close to enlightenment.
fix.replace: The measure of [each] merit is [as much as the merit] of all beings, excluding Bodhisattvas who are close to enlightenment,

note: Accurate Abhidharmakośa material on obstructing karma and the bodhisattva's mark-producing karma; the last sentence inverts the exclusion.
Faithful rendering of the synonyms of the dharmadhātu and the gloss of dhātu as gotra.

errors.english: The Blessed One said: "The Perfection of Wisdom is not something to be exerted upon,"
errors.why: bcom ldan 'das is a vocative: the sūtra cites Subhūti addressing the Lord ('Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom...'), as the translator correctly took it earlier on the side.

fix.find: The Blessed One said: "The Perfection of Wisdom
fix.replace: the text says: "Blessed One, the Perfection of Wisdom

errors.why: 'This' is the proposed (non-pervasive) definition of buddhavacana, not an inconsistency.

errors.english: Because it is difficult and involves suffering, one must have great faith
errors.why: The gloss explains that it is hard to have faith in (one believes in it only with difficulty and pain), not that one must have great faith.

note: Good on the four causes of abandoning the Dharma and the colophon; the sūtra citation misidentifies the speaker.

errors.english: If a Buddha or a Bodhisattva who practices the supreme conduct of mantra is exhorted according to the described method, yet the goal is not accomplished, it would constitute a transgression of the vow
errors.why: It is the practitioner of the supreme mantra conduct who urges; the buddha or bodhisattva who, so urged, does not grant accomplishment is the one who transgresses the samaya.

note: A difficult word-commentary rendered mostly plausibly, but who urges and who transgresses is blurred in places.

errors.english: Undoubtedly, the nature of reality is not exactly like that.
errors.why: The Tibetan affirms: 'undoubtedly it is just so', because the ultimate and the conventional exist in mutual dependence.

fix.find: Undoubtedly, the nature of reality is not exactly like that.

note: Sound rendering of the specific and general characteristics of the afflictions; the opening sentence is negated.

errors.english: the substance called (sarala) pine resin, (ko-nyon-tse) an unidentified herbal ingredient
errors.why: ko nyon tse is the Tibetan name for the ingredient called sarala, one item, not two.

errors.english: (mukaka) likely a species of wood apple or similar medicinal plant
errors.why: The muṣkaka group is named after muṣkaka (mokṣaka, Schrebera), not a wood apple.

note: A careful rendering of the kapha-type recipes and the alkali preparation; minor issues in the list of materia medica.

errors.english: At the site of the student
errors.why: bdag po'i gnas is the place of the lord, the same term just rendered 'sites of the five masters'; 'student' is unsupported.

note: Accurate sequence of mantras and mudrās for binding the directions; one place-term mistranslated.
